summary: Triggers an action on the current screen: save, submit, create, open a dialog. If it takes the user somewhere else, it is a link, not a button.
whenToUse: The user commits an action on this screen: Save, Submit, Create project, Approve.
Primary: the one action you most want the user to take in this view. One per form, dialog or page section.
Secondary: the alternatives sitting next to the primary, like Cancel or Save as draft.
Ghost: low-emphasis actions repeated in lists, tables or toolbars (Edit, View diff), where a row of filled buttons would fight for attention.
Size sm in dense places: table rows, card footers, toolbars. Size md everywhere else.
whenNotToUse: Going to another page or URL: use a text link. Links and buttons are announced differently and users expect Cmd+click to open links in a new tab.
Turning a setting on or off: use a switch or a checkbox (not in the system yet, open an issue).
More than three actions in one row: keep the main ones and move the rest to an overflow menu.

dos.title: Start the label with a verb that says what happens
dos.text: "Save changes" and "Publish release" tell the user the outcome before they click.

dos.title: One primary per view, the others step down
dos.text: Hierarchy tells users where to look first. Secondary and ghost carry the alternatives.

dos.title: Show progress with loading, keep the label
dos.text: The button stays in place and focusable, so keyboard users do not lose their position.

donts.title: Two primary buttons side by side
donts.text: When everything is primary, nothing is. Users hesitate and pick at random.

donts.title: Vague labels
donts.text: "OK" and "Click here" say nothing out of context, and screen reader users often list buttons out of context.

donts.title: Ghost for the main action of a form
donts.text: Without a container it reads as optional. Users scroll past it looking for the real button.

accessibility: It is a native button: Enter and Space work, it is in the tab order, and no extra ARIA is needed.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width) only appears for keyboard focus, never on mouse click.
Loading sets aria-busy and ignores clicks, but keeps the button focusable so keyboard users keep their place.
Disabled removes the button from the tab order and is not explained to anyone. Prefer an enabled button plus a message saying what is missing.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label: the visible text is the accessible name, so without text there is no name.
Height is 40px (md) and 32px (sm). Both pass the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size of 24px; prefer md on touch screens.
